title: Pluggable event reconstructor and idempotent rehydration tool for analytics backfills
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Purpose: Build a reusable, pluggable event reconstructor and idempotent rehydration tool that can perform targeted backfills and partial replays against the Console analytics warehouse and metrics streams. Scope: support windowed rehydration, schema-migration-safe transformations, checkpointed progress, per-tenant scoping, and cost-aware execution. The tool must operate as a standalone operator that can be invoked ad-hoc or orchestrated from existing backfill pipelines. It should emit rich progress and failure telemetry and provide a dry-run mode for validation before writes.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can replay a 24-hour partition for a single customer with at-most-once writes disabled and produce idempotent events into the analytics write API
Checkpoints persisted every 5 minutes and resume correctly after simulated process termination
Schema migration path: reconstructor can apply a transformation map to convert historical events to current analytics schema with at least two-example unit tests
Dry-run validates produced rows against current ingestion validation and produces a report of diffs without mutating the warehouse
End-to-end run emits metrics: processed_events, replays_succeeded, replays_failed, write_retries, peak_memory_mb, estimated_cost_usd
Integration test coverage that replays 1M synthetic events within staging and verifies deduplication and ordering semantics
design_notes: Architecture: pluggable stages (reader -> normalizer -> transformer -> deduper -> writer). Each stage exposes a well-defined interface so future readers (e.g., S3, Kafka, archival store) can be added without touching core logic.

Idempotency: use a composite idempotency key composed of (source_stream, event_id, schema_version). Writers will be responsible for conditional upserts in the analytics write API to guarantee idempotent apply semantics.

Checkpointing: store checkpoints in the existing replay-checkpoints DynamoDB table with a generation token to avoid zombie replays overlapping. Checkpoint granularity configurable per run (time or count).
Backpressure: writer stage exposes a token-bucket control and the scheduler uses adaptive parallelism based on current write latency SLO targets to avoid overwhelming downstream warehouse.
Transformations: transformation maps are small YAML files checked into infra repo; transformations executed in a sandboxed Python worker to allow safe migration logic and unit tests.
Cost controls: support estimated_cost cap and early stop if projected cost exceeds budget; provide a staged run that first computes cost estimate before writes.
Observability: emit event-level sampling logs plus aggregate progress metrics and detailed failure reasons to Sentry/Tracing with replay run id tags. Expose per-tenant percent-complete and ETA.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge prototype behind feature flag to staging; 2) Run dry-run for small customers (5 tenants) and validate reports; 3) Run gradual backfills for larger tenants with cost caps; 4) Monitor metrics for increased write latencies and rollback if >10% SLA degradation; 5) Promote to prod and enable self-serve UI in Console for approved ops users.
updates: 2026-03-10: Created ticket; initial design sketched and sprint slot requested.
2026-03-11: Spike implemented for reader/transformer interface; prototype can read S3 archives and produce normalized events. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-proto/pull/97
2026-03-12: Design review with analytics and infra; request to add generation token to checkpointing and require transformation sandboxing. Added tests for idempotency key collisions.
2026-03-13: Benchmarked writer stage on staging: 20k events/s with batch size 500; memory spike observed when parallelism >= 16. Blocking: need adaptive parallelism throttle (ENG-61852 created).
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for each stage with synthetic events including schema-versioned payloads; 2) Integration test that runs a full dry-run against a staging S3 bucket and verifies diff report; 3) Chaos test: kill operator during run and ensure checkpoint resumes without duplication; 4) Load test: replay 2M events in staging and assert memory and CPU remain within thresholds; 5) Security review on transformation sandbox codepaths before prod.
estimated_cost_impact: Moderate: backfills will increase S3 egress and writer compute; initial projection for a single 30-day tenant backfill is ~$450-900 depending on batching and transformation overhead.
notes_for_ops: Provide run-book: how to pause/cancel runs, how to inspect checkpoints, how to run dry-run, and how to escalate write-failure anomalies. Include sample CLI commands and recommended feature flags to toggle behavior.
next_steps: Complete transformation sandbox with unit test harness
Add conditional upsert support to analytics write API (coord with backend team)
